method.name: milp_aggregate_production
steps: Decision variables (all integer for counting units): produce[t], outsource[t], hire[t], fire[t], workforce[t], inventory[t], backorder[t]; continuous: regular_hours[t], overtime_hours[t].
Workforce balance: workforce[t] = workforce[t-1] + hire[t] - fire[t]; workforce[0]=1000.
Regular hours: regular_hours[t] = 160 * workforce[t]; paid 30/hr regardless of utilization.
Labor for production: 5 * produce[t] <= regular_hours[t] + overtime_hours[t].
Inventory balance: inventory[t] = inventory[t-1] + produce[t] + outsource[t] - demand[t] - backorder[t]; inventory[0]=15000.
Backorder: backorder[t] = max(0, demand[t] + backorder[t-1] - produce[t] - outsource[t] - inventory[t-1]).
Revenue: 300 * sold[t]; sold[t] = min(inventory[t-1] + produce[t] + outsource[t], demand[t] + backorder[t-1]).

Costs: raw_material 90*produce[t]; outsourcing 200*outsource[t]; holding 15*inventory[t]; backorder 35*backorder[t]; hire 5000*hire[t]; fire 8000*fire[t]; regular_wage 30*regular_hours[t]; overtime 40*overtime_hours[t].
Objective: maximize total net profit = sum_t (revenue - all costs).

method.name: milp_aggregate_production_v2
steps: Same as milp_aggregate_production but use explicit sold[t] and available[t] variables to linearize the min() fulfillment logic.
available[t] = inventory[t-1] + produce[t] + outsource[t]; requirement[t] = demand[t] + backorder[t-1];

sold[t] <= available[t]; sold[t] <= requirement[t]; sold[t] >= available[t] + requirement[t] - M*(1-y[t]) with binary y[t]; OR simpler: sold[t] = available[t] - max(0, available[t] - requirement[t]); inventory[t] = max(0, available[t] - requirement[t]); backorder[t] = max(0, requirement[t] - available[t]).
These max() linearizations use big-M or additional variables to stay MILP.
All other constraints same as v1.
Integer: produce, outsource, hire, fire, workforce, inventory, backorder, sold, y (if used).
